reason: At base, the REGEX_FORMAT matches Y{1,4} but format() only implements YY and YYYY; unmatched tokens fall through to the timezone-offset fallback, so format('Y') returns a UTC offset like '+0000' instead of the literal 'Y', and format('YYY') similarly falls through.

At head, the PR changes REGEX_FORMAT to only match YYYY|YY (not Y{1,4}), so unsupported tokens like Y and YYY are preserved literally instead of falling through to the timezone offset. The diff also shows explicit test assertions for Y and YYY that pass.

The PR is a pure refactoring that extracts tryDecodeURIComponent into a shared utility. The existing code in request.ts already decoded percent-encoded route parameters correctly; the refactor just deduplicates the logic without changing behavior.
Same refactoring PR as js_0011 applied at head. The percent-decoding behavior for route parameters is unchanged; the code was just reorganized into a shared utility function.

At base, SortedEntry#reschedule writes the new score to Redis via zincrby but never updates @score in memory, so entry.score and entry.at return stale (pre-reschedule) values. The test expects the in-memory score to reflect the new time.
At head, the fix adds '@score = at.to_f' after the zincrby call, keeping the in-memory score in sync with Redis. The test's assertion that entry.score matches the new time will pass.

The PR modifies parseRangesSpecifier for Range header whitespace handling in ktor-http. Content-Type header parsing with charset parameters is in a completely unrelated subsystem, so the test behavior is unchanged at base.
Same Range header whitespace PR at head. Content-Type parsing with charset parameters is unaffected by this change.
The PR only changes error message formatting in ComposerRepository (adding filename to warning/exception messages). Archive timestamp preservation is completely unrelated to this logging change.
Same logging-only PR at head. Archive timestamp behavior is unaffected by error message formatting changes.

The PR changes CredentialCache prefix path comparison to be case-sensitive (in System.Net.Primitives). JSON deserialization with nullable parent properties is in an entirely unrelated subsystem (System.Text.Json).
Same CredentialCache PR at head. JSON deserialization behavior is completely unaffected by URI prefix matching changes.
The PR fixes FETCH FIRST on empty WITH HOLD cursors in sql_cursor.go. INET type operations and <<= ANY comparisons are completely unrelated to cursor fetch handling.
Same cursor fix PR at head. INET >>= ANY operations are unaffected by cursor fetch behavior changes.

At base, the proxy-environment parsing always treats NO_PROXY entries as domain names, prefixing them with a wildcard. An IPv6 entry like '::1' is wrongly transformed into a pattern that causes an error during client construction.
At head, the fix adds is_ipv4_hostname and is_ipv6_hostname checks, handling '::1' as an IPv6 address with proper bracket notation 'all://[::1]'. Client construction succeeds.

At base, the code in Series.str.match compiles the pattern with the full flag set, then checks if flags match exactly. Passing flags=re.DOTALL (for dot-matches-newline) raises a ValueError because the reconstructed flag set fails the strict equality check.

At head, the fix changes the flag comparison to only check IGNORECASE (since that's the only flag case can contribute), allowing DOTALL and other flags to pass through. The DOTALL flag is properly applied and 'a\nc' matches 'a.c'.

At base, prepare_steps doesn't update prev_task and prev_res after processing a group in the middle of a chain. When the chain has a group followed by more tasks, subsequent tasks incorrectly link back to tasks before the group, causing serialization to lose child results.

At head, the fix adds code to update prev_task and prev_res after processing a group, so subsequent tasks correctly link to the last task in the group. Serialization preserves all child results across both groups.

At base, when the parser encounters -- and the current positional does NOT have allow_hyphen_values, it unconditionally enters trailing-values mode, ignoring the positional's value_terminator. So '--' is treated as the escape sequence rather than as the value_terminator, causing all remaining tokens including --check to be consumed by the first positional.

At head, the fix adds a check: if the current positional has a value_terminator matching the token, let the positional handle it instead of entering trailing-values mode. This allows '--' to act as the value_terminator, correctly handing off --check to the second positional.

At base, the code uses vim.api.nvim_set_option_value('background', bg, {}) which triggers OptionSet when not starting up. Since the test sets up autocommands after startup and the terminal color change happens later, OptionSet fires. ColorScheme also fires as a side effect of the background change.

At head, the fix replaces nvim_set_option_value with vim.cmd('noautocmd set background=' .. bg), which explicitly suppresses all autocommands including OptionSet. The test expects OptionSet to fire, but it no longer does.

The PR only reorders checks in Ecto.Schema's compile-time @derive attribute handling to avoid unnecessary compile-time dependencies. Required field validation and changeset validity are runtime behaviors completely unaffected by this compile-time optimization.
Same compile-time dependency optimization PR at head. Changeset validation behavior is unaffected by the order in which @derive attributes are read during compilation.
